Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a chemical cross-linking (CXMS) study using the BS3 linker to map interactions between NOSIP and TNPO1. The acquisition mode is clearly DDA (Top25). While the protein NOSIP is described as an E3-ubiquitin ligase, the proteomics assay itself is not an enrichment for ubiquitin remnants, but rather a cross-linking analysis of a purified complex.

scope: His-NOSIP, 20 µM, and 20 µM His-TNPO1 were incubated for 2 h on ice in a total volume of 300 µl, and complexes were purified using a Superdex S200 analytical 10/300 GL column
Complex-containing fractions were pooled and cross-linked using bis(sulfosuccinimidyl)suberate (BS3, Thermo Fisher, A39266, dissolved in dimethyl sulfoxide)
Cross-linked complexes were subjected to SDS-PAGE (NuPAGE gradient 4–12%), and shifted bands in the gel corresponding to TNPO1 cross-linked to NOSIP were cut out and analyzed

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on a purified complex of His-NOSIP and His-TNPO1 that was further isolated via size exclusion chromatography and SDS-PAGE band excision.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry portion of this study is a structural characterization experiment using chemical cross-linking (XL-MS) to map the interaction interface between NOSIP and TNPO1. It is not a differential proteomics study comparing treated vs control groups, nor a perturbation study. Therefore, it is classified as 'un-classified' per the fallback rules for non-perturbation studies.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a chemical cross-linking (CXMS) experiment. Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the cross-linked peptides without a specialized search engine like pLink or a CXMS-aware modifier. The analysis is site-centric (identifying specific lysine-lysine cross-links).
